text:
Marathon Petroleum shares rose modestly today after two days of sharp declines, as oil prices climbed on Wednesday following reports that the U.S. is preparing potential strikes against Iran. With crude trading near $108 per barrel and geopolitical tensions escalating, refiners benefit from higher oil prices when they can pass costs through to refined products—though the real driver of the recent selloff appears to be behind the stock now, with peace talk signals on October 27th having knocked shares down nearly $35 in two days.

The refiner is operating at 93.4% capacity into relatively full storage tanks, which limits its ability to capture outsized margins during price spikes. The ongoing cost of the Iran conflict and talk of Russian diesel entering the market add to near-term headwinds for refining margins, even as geopolitical premiums keep crude prices elevated.
